title: Before and After: The First Oil Wells

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *antes de que* and *después de que* from B2 Unit 7: *antes de que* is always followed by the subjunctive, and *después de que* takes the indicative for what happened and the subjunctive for what is still to come. The first oil wells divide the history of Venezuela into a before and an after, so the two connectors fit the topic.

sections.title: Before and after
rows: Antes de que se descubriera el petróleo, Venezuela vivía del café y del cacao.
*antes de que* + imperfect subjunctive after a past verb
Después de que se abrió el pozo, llegaron muchas empresas.
Antes de que llegue la lluvia, cerramos las válvulas.
*antes de que* + present subjunctive: it has not happened yet
Después de que termine la visita, hablaremos del petróleo.
*después de que* + subjunctive: still to come

items.spanish: Antes de que se descubriera el petróleo, Venezuela vivía del café y del cacao.
items.english: Before oil was discovered, Venezuela lived from coffee and cacao.

items.spanish: Después de que se abrió el pozo, llegaron muchas empresas.
items.english: After the well was opened, many companies arrived.

items.spanish: Antes de que llegara la empresa, el pueblo era tranquilo.
items.english: Before the company arrived, the village was quiet.

items.spanish: Hablaremos después de que termine la visita.
items.english: We will talk after the visit ends.

sections.content: Two questions decide everything. After *antes de que* the verb is always in the subjunctive: *antes de que llegara*, never *antes de que llegó*. After *después de que* ask whether it has happened: yes means indicative, not yet means subjunctive. If the same person does both actions, use the infinitive: *antes de salir*.
